stay: During 2025, the Bank was hit with regulatory investigations, two putative class-action lawsuits and civil money penalties arising from its overdraft fee practices.

Customers, two state attorneys general and a former supplier have brought claims, investigations and lawsuits against the Company relating to the 2024 data security incident.
Since the merger, the Group has remained in litigation, arbitration and mediation with the former owners of Halvorsen Marine over the calculation of the earn-out payment.
The Corporation is currently defending litigation, regulatory proceedings and claims by customers, and it expects its defense costs to remain elevated through 2026.

Throughout the year Northwind Logistics LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary, was named as a defendant in wage-and-hour lawsuits, misclassification claims and administrative proceedings brought by current and former drivers.
Management has recorded a litigation reserve of $18.4 million for the consolidated patent infringement actions pending against the Company in the District of Delaware.
The Partnership incurred $6.2 million of defense costs during 2025 in connection with legal proceedings, regulatory inquiries and landowner claims arising from the Clearwater pipeline release.
Kestrel Energy Partners was sued in March 2025 by a group of royalty owners alleging underpayment of royalties, and the lawsuit remains in discovery.
In 2025 the Firm and several other financial institutions were named as defendants in antitrust lawsuits alleging manipulation of benchmark rates, and the Firm intends to defend itself vigorously.
Several former employees filed a putative class action against Tamarind Health in 2024, and that litigation, together with a parallel Department of Labor investigation, remains pending.
The Partnership resolved the last outstanding legal claim arising from the 2022 compressor station explosion during the year, paying $2.3 million in excess of insurance recoveries.

Lawsuits, arbitrations and governmental investigations involving the Firm's commodities trading business remained pending at year-end, and the Firm increased its reserves for those matters by $35 million.

The Corporation and certain of its current and former officers are defendants in a consolidated securities class action and in related shareholder derivative lawsuits filed after the 2024 restatement.
Brightwater Utilities has been the target of lawsuits, municipal claims and challenges by rate-case intervenors since the wildfire in its northern service territory.
Following the dam failure, residents, insurers and two counties commenced legal proceedings against the Group, and management estimates that losses could exceed the $120 million accrued to date.
No trial date has been set in the antitrust litigation brought against the Company by a coalition of independent pharmacies, and discovery is ongoing.

At December 31, 2025, the Bank's accrued liabilities included litigation reserves of $64 million, principally for mortgage repurchase demands, servicing-related lawsuits and an employment arbitration.
In the third quarter, the Company was served with a lawsuit by a former reseller alleging breach of contract and tortious interference and seeking damages of approximately $15 million.
Marlowe Foods prevailed at trial in its trademark litigation against a competitor in June 2025; the jury awarded damages of $4.1 million, and the verdict is under appeal.
The Partnership lost its appeal in the contract litigation with the former operator of its gathering system and paid the $11.7 million judgment, plus accrued interest, in the second quarter.
Pending against the Corporation are numerous asbestos-related lawsuits, environmental claims and premises liability actions, most of which allege exposure at facilities closed before 1990.
In addition to the matters described above, the Firm is involved in other legal proceedings, regulatory reviews and arbitrations arising in connection with the conduct of its businesses.
Veridian Logistics was hit with lawsuits, investigations and penalties after the collapse of its Memphis distribution center, and its insurers have reserved their rights with respect to coverage.

Late in the year the Company received a demand letter from a former licensee asserting royalty underpayments, and the licensee has stated that it will commence litigation if the dispute is not resolved by March 2026.
Harborview Financial added $5 million to its litigation reserves in the fourth quarter after the court granted class certification in the mortgage escrow case brought by its borrowers.
In Brazil the Group's subsidiary, Solace Farmaceutica Ltda., is a party to labor lawsuits, tax assessments and civil proceedings, for which it has recorded provisions of R$38 million.
The Company is a defendant in thirty-two lawsuits alleging injuries from its discontinued surgical mesh product and has accrued a loss contingency equal to the low end of its estimated range of loss.
Our company faced litigation, regulatory proceedings and fines in 2025 stemming from the mislabeling of certain dietary supplements, and it paid $3.2 million to resolve the regulatory matters.
Within the commercial banking segment, the Bank settled lender liability claims, a fraudulent transfer action and a related lawsuit brought by a bankruptcy trustee for a combined $8 million.
The Corporation's former chief executive officer commenced an arbitration and a separate lawsuit against the Corporation seeking severance benefits, and both proceedings remain pending.
Throughout 2025 management devoted significant resources to the defense of the Company in the opioid litigation, related governmental investigations and insurance coverage disputes.

Disputes with three general contractors over cost overruns on the Riverside plant expansion have resulted in liens, arbitration demands and legal claims against the Partnership totaling approximately $27 million.
Aldridge Industries' Canadian subsidiary was fined and then sued by provincial environmental authorities following a 2024 tailings spill, and that litigation remains ongoing.

In May 2025 a former franchisee initiated a legal proceeding against the Company in Texas state court, alleging fraudulent inducement and seeking rescission of its franchise agreement.
Management continues to defend the Group against customer claims, regulatory investigations and lawsuits, and it has accrued amounts for those matters it considers probable and reasonably estimable.
The Corporation has accrued loss contingencies totaling $73 million for the environmental, product liability and employment matters pending against it, as described in this note.

leave: The Company classifies legal fees, including those relating to litigation, as selling, general and administrative expenses and recognizes them as incurred.

We engage outside counsel to advise us on securities, tax, intellectual property and litigation matters, and we recognize their fees in general and administrative expense as the services are rendered.

A loss contingency is accrued when information available before the financial statements are issued indicates that it is probable that a liability has been incurred and the amount of the loss can be reasonably estimated.
Legal costs expected to be incurred in connection with loss contingencies are expensed as incurred and are not included in the measurement of the related liability.

As defined in the credit agreement, Consolidated EBITDA means consolidated net income plus, to the extent deducted in arriving at net income, interest expense, income taxes, depreciation and amortization, non-cash stock compensation, and fees and expenses relating to litigation settlements, restructurings and permitted acquisitions.

We define Adjusted EBITDA as net income before interest, income taxes, depreciation and amortization, further adjusted to exclude stock-based compensation, restructuring charges, impairment charges and changes in litigation reserves.

Other operating expenses comprise occupancy, communications, travel, consulting, insurance and litigation-related costs, as well as other costs that are not allocated to a specific functional line item.

The Partnership's insurance program includes commercial general liability, pollution legal liability, and directors' and officers' liability policies, which generally cover defense costs and settlements of covered legal claims above specified self-insured retentions.

Under its indemnification agreements with directors and officers, the Corporation has agreed to indemnify them, to the fullest extent permitted by Delaware law, against expenses, judgments and amounts paid in settlement of legal proceedings arising from their service to the Corporation.

In the ordinary course of business, the Company enters into agreements with customers, suppliers and service providers that include indemnification provisions covering third-party legal claims, such as claims of intellectual property infringement.

Estimates and assumptions are used in accounting for, among other things, allowances for credit losses, the valuation of goodwill and intangible assets, uncertain tax positions, and the probability and amount of loss contingencies.

Factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from our forward-looking statements include changes in interest rates, competition, cybersecurity incidents, changes in tax laws, the costs and effects of litigation generally, and severe weather.
Professional fees include amounts paid to auditors, tax advisers, actuaries, investment bankers and attorneys for transactional, compliance and litigation support services.

The Group's policy is to recognize a provision for legal claims only when it has a present obligation as a result of a past event, an outflow of resources is probable, and the amount can be estimated reliably.

Under the revolving credit agreement, events of default include, among other things, nonpayment, breach of covenants, a change of control, and the entry of final judgments in litigation exceeding $50 million that remain unpaid and unstayed for 60 consecutive days.

The Bank's directors' and officers' liability insurance provides coverage, subject to policy limits and retentions, for losses arising from lawsuits alleging wrongful acts by directors and officers in their capacities as such.
We expense the costs of defending lawsuits, responding to regulatory inquiries and enforcing our intellectual property rights as incurred.

In assessing whether a loss contingency should be accrued, management considers factors such as the procedural posture of a matter, the advice of counsel, and the outcomes of similar matters involving other companies.
Litigation, adverse regulatory action and unanticipated competition are examples of events that could indicate that the carrying amount of a long-lived asset may not be recoverable.

Contingent consideration, environmental remediation obligations and loss contingencies assumed in a business combination are recognized at fair value at the acquisition date if fair value can be determined during the measurement period.
Amounts recoverable from insurers with respect to litigation and other claims are recognized as an asset only when recovery is probable, and are presented separately from the related liabilities.

Legal costs incurred to successfully defend our patents are capitalized as part of the carrying amount of the patent, while the costs of unsuccessful defenses and of any litigation in which we are named as a defendant are expensed as incurred.
The Partnership's lease agreements require lessees to maintain liability insurance and to indemnify the Partnership against legal claims arising from their use of the leased properties.
Disclosure of a loss contingency is not required when the likelihood of loss is remote, unless the contingency arises from a guarantee.
The credit agreement permits add-backs to EBITDA for non-recurring legal settlements and litigation expenses, not to exceed $25 million in any period of four consecutive fiscal quarters.
